title: Patriots Limit A.J. Brown’s Practice Return, Rule Out Three Players – NBC Sports Update
body:
The New England Patriots entered their first overseas matchup of the season with a mixed health report on Wednesday, confirming that three players will be unavailable for Sunday’s game against the Detroit Lions in Munich while offering a glimmer of optimism about the status of wide receiver A.J. Brown. The Patriots’ medical staff ruled out linebacker Matt Cox, safety Devin McCourty and cornerback Jalen Reed for the international contest, citing lingering injuries that require continued rest. Meanwhile, Brown, who missed the majority of the past two weeks with a hamstring strain, participated in a limited capacity during Tuesday’s practice, suggesting he may be close to full participation when the team takes the field under the lights of the Olympiastadion.

The three absences represent a notable blow to New England’s defensive depth. Cox, a versatile linebacker who has been a key contributor on special teams and in sub‑package blitzes, suffered a high‑ankle sprain in the previous week’s win over the Buffalo Bills. McCourty, the veteran safety and team captain, is dealing with a lingering shoulder issue that has limited his snap count, while Reed’s lingering calf strain has kept him out of recent drills. Head coach Bill Belichick, known for his meticulous preparation, emphasized that the Patriots will rely on younger players and recent signings to fill the gaps, noting that the team’s “next‑man‑up” culture is being tested on a global stage.

The limited practice involvement of A.J. Brown, however, provides a counterbalance to the defensive setbacks. Brown, who was acquired in the offseason to add a deep‑threat dimension to the Patriots’ passing attack, has been sidelined since early October after a Grade 2 hamstring strain was diagnosed during a routine conditioning session. On Tuesday, he completed a series of short routes and a series of non‑contact drills before being pulled after ten minutes. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels said the session was “a good sign” and that Brown’s “muscle response is exactly what we hoped to see.” If Brown is cleared for Sunday, he could stretch the Lions’ secondary and open up the Patriots’ short‑and‑intermediate passing game, which has struggled to find consistency this season.

The Lions, meanwhile, are approaching the game with a relatively healthy roster. Their starting quarterback, Jared Goff, is fully cleared, and the defensive line boasts a full complement of starters after a week of intensive recovery work. The international fixture is the first regular‑season NFL game ever played in Germany, and both clubs are aware of the added pressure of representing the league on a global platform. Analysts predict that New England’s offensive line will be the decisive factor, as they must protect the quarterback while allowing Brown the time to develop his routes.

Beyond the immediate tactical considerations, the Patriots’ situation underscores the broader challenges of an NFL season that now stretches across continents. Travel fatigue, time‑zone adjustments and limited practice windows can exacerbate existing injuries, forcing coaching staffs to make swift roster decisions. Belichick’s reliance on depth players could pay dividends if the younger talent steps up, but the loss of seasoned veterans on defense may limit the team’s ability to generate turnovers—a hallmark of New England’s traditional identity.

Looking ahead, the Patriots will aim to finish the first half of the season with a winning record, and a victory in Munich would be a significant morale boost. The health of A.J. Brown will be a focal point for fans and pundits alike; his potential return could revitalize a passing game that has been underwhelming. Conversely, the defensive holes left by Cox, McCourty and Reed will need to be addressed quickly, either through internal adjustments or strategic signings before the next round of games. As the league continues to expand its global footprint, New England’s performance in Germany could set the tone for how teams manage player health and depth in an increasingly demanding schedule.
